name: Port Daddy Fleet
description: Port Daddy's fleet is a small crew of background agents — a reviewer, a red-teamer, a QA, a test-author, a tautology-checker, a dead-code unspider, a documentarian — that watch the repository the way a harbormaster watches a port. The fleet doesn't open PRs at you uninvited. It waits until something moves: a commit lands, a PR opens, a check fails. Then the relevant ship leaves drydock, does one small specific thing (read the diff, ask a hard question, propose a fix, write the test that was missing), and posts what it saw back to the right GitHub surface under a per-ship identity so you can tell at a glance who's talking. Each ship signs as itself. Killing the fleet (`pd fleet down`) doesn't uninstall the App; the App stays installed but quiet, which is the right default for a thing that has commit rights to your repos.
